newsitem.title: USA: No Sprint stock for new entrant of Global One.
newsitem.headline: No Sprint stock for new entrant of Global One.

text.p: Sprint Corp. said Tuesday it does not plan to offer an equity stake in the parent telecommunications company to any Asian partner which joins its Global One alliance with France Telecom and Deutsche Telekom AG.
"We haven't seen the need to increase that equity," Kevin Brauer, president of Sprint Business, told Reuters. "Remember, we have a standstill agreement with our European partners."
The French and German partners each have a 10 percent stake in Sprint, and the alliance is scrambling to secure the best Asian partners to plug gaps in its strength and beat its archrival, Concert.
Concert is the name for British Telecommunications Plc and MCI Communications Corp., which agreed to merge in November.
The standstill agreement limits the ability of Sprint to issue new shares without the permission of its partners.
Brauer declined to say which Asian partner Sprint is looking for, but analysts believe both Global One and Concert want to get NTT Corp., the main Japanese national telephone carrier, as a partner.
The European Union on Tuesday gave final approval to the Global One alliance, helping Sprint shares rise $2 to $44.625 on the New York Stock Exchange.
Brauer said he was confident Global One would meet the its 1997 revenue target of $1.3 billion, which follows annualized 1996 revenues of $800 million.
However, he conceded the company had exceeded 1996 budgets, though he declined to say by how much or why.
Sources close to Global One told Reuters last month the venture had lost $370 million, instead of the $250 million budgeted.
"From the original budget that was put in, yes (we did exceed it)," Brauer said. He also said some Global One headquarters staff employees were being cut, but would give no details.
"The employees have been told today, I believe," he said.
Global One had 2,900 employeees at the end of 1996, with about 200 at its corporate headquarters in Brussels.
However Brauer emphasised that, overall, Global One would employ 500 more people in a year's time than it does now.
